newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: The South African industrial and all-share indices finished at record closing highs in active trade on Thursday, boosted by a host of positive news.

Dealers said that two upbeat sets of economic data, namely the far higher-than-expected May trade surplus of 1.75 billion rand released earlier and Wednesday's lower-than-forecast May consumer inflation figure, had cheered the market.
The announcement that private individuals may invest 200,000 rand offshore from July 1, well above the 160,000 limit anticipated by the market, had also boosted sentiment.
A rally on the futures market had helped to propel industrial stocks, aiding the industrial index to a record finish of 8,742.3 a gain of 72.4 points and a level last seen on January 25, 1996.
"The market is particularly strong. There has been lots of futures play. Everything is just positive. There is no bad news," a dealer said.
Dealers said futures were lifted by bond market strength where yields fell to their lowest levels in 16 months.
In late trade September industrial futures were some 150 points stronger at 8,605/10 from 8,453 before.
The jovial mood held gold shares steady despite a slightly weaker bullion price. The index gained 1.4 points 1,008.8.
On the overall market, the all-share index was pushed up 48.7 points to its third consecutive closing high at 7,402.7. Near month all-share futures were sturdy at 6,822/35 from 6,743 overnight.
In the broader, market advancing issues lead decliners by 211 to 157 with 145 shares unchanged. Thirty-four new highs were recorded compared to 17 new lows.
The market was seen taking a breather on Friday although the underlying tone was seen still firm and the approaching unit trust close-out was expected to lift prices.

"We must bear in mind that the unit trust quarter end is approaching on Friday. The firm trend will continue tomorrow with a bit of profit-taking," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters.
Some "massaging" of prices was seen on Friday and Monday.
"The funds are bunched very closely together and every bit of performance you can get will make a lot of difference in rankings," one dealer said.
Some funds end their quarters on Friday while others sign off on Monday.

Among key market features Randgold tumbled 300 cents to a year low of 23 rand amid disappointment following a much lower-than-expected listing price set for its resources unit which made its debut in London on Thursday.
Randgold managing director Mark Bristow, however, said that the outcome of the listing was satisfactory considering the recent adverse circumstances in the gold market.
These included gold's downturn to below $340 and the continuing impact of the Bre-X scandal, where a Canadian junior exploration firm vastly overstated the potential of a gold find in Indonesia.
Insurance and banking firm RMB Holdings added 10 cents to 13.20 rand following a bookover deal of 2.3 million shares worth around 29 million rand.
New Clicks was unchanged at 495 cents in heavy volume worth 20.3 million rand boosted by an early foreign trade deal.
-- Charles Phahlane, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
